verdict_text: YES. The plan deletes exactly the 48 buffers, upcasts everything to float32, casts exactly the 64 named projection matrices to bfloat16 (float16 to float32 to bfloat16 equals a direct cast, as the spec allows), keeps names unchanged, and writes a sharded safetensors output with a 256 MiB limit. The required checks are all present as asserts: the "exactly 64 bfloat16" check is implemented as the conjunction of "the 64 matrices are bfloat16" and "every other tensor is float32", which is logically equivalent and fails loudly if any other tensor were bfloat16; the layer-0 query_key_value, embed_in and 196-count checks are asserted literally.
